stage: the no-control route, arm A1 — I2V from a start frame rendered from the GLB
registered_by: executor seat, on E11-nocontrol, before the first submission of any E11 graph
how_these_were_chosen: The date as a plain integer with a run index appended, continuing the rule specs/E08-seeds.json, specs/E09-A3-seeds.json and specs/E10-seeds.json use: 2026-08-12, runs 31, 32 and 33. The property that matters is that all three numbers are fixed BEFORE any result is seen, and a date-derived seed is checkable against this file's own git timestamp. None was drawn from a prior run, from any served template, or from anything this seat had already looked at.

allocation.2026081231: the probe — the one generation this spec authorises up front
allocation.2026081232: reserve, spendable only on a named cause the probe surfaces

why_the_index_starts_at_31: specs/E09-A3-seeds.json registered 2026081201-02, specs/E08-seeds.json registered 2026081211-13 and specs/E10-seeds.json registered 2026081221-22 on this same calendar day. Reusing any of those numbers would put a seed registered for one experiment onto another, and the record would afterwards have to explain which run a number belonged to. The offset keeps every seed on this rig traceable to exactly one registration.
why_a_new_seed_and_not_E08_s: E11 runs a different model family (Wan 2.2 I2V-A14B, two experts) through a different conditioning node on a differently-shaped latent path, and its high-noise sampler is a KSamplerAdvanced rather than E08's KSampler. The same integer would not reproduce E08's noise field even in principle, so registering a fresh number states that plainly rather than implying a same-seed comparison the route cannot deliver. E10's report records the same rider for the frame-count case.
the_two_seed_reading_rule: E10's closing ruling R3 stands and E11 is read under it from birth: a scene observation from ONE seed is an observation, never a route property. The probe registered here is one seed, so nothing this experiment reports about the scene may be written as a property of the route. The reserves are what a second seed would be drawn from, on a named cause and the advisor's call, not this seat's.
ceiling: 3 generations wave 1 — 1 probe plus 2 reserve on named causes. estimate_credits is recorded before the first submission and both meters are reported; on an all-OSS graph it returns 0 by construction (E08 section 12), so the ceiling is enforced by counting generations. Spent credits have no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/gates.py::gate_s_seed_registration enforces both clauses at build time and tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces them again against the graph that is about to run, on the saved file the cloud actually executes.
the_inert_second_seed: The low-noise expert's KSamplerAdvanced carries noise_seed 0 with add_noise=disable. It draws nothing, so it is inert; route_gates.gate_s_registration reports it and does not demand it be registered. Recorded here so a reader of the graph does not find an unregistered 0 and take it for a gap in this list.
